evidence.quote: We are adopting Zypherion for the analytics pipeline.

observations.why: The declarative adoption presents a decision as authorized and settled, but supplies no named organizational role or process.
A quantified comparative performance claim supplies expertise-coded evidence and an argument for the choice.
A fixed near-term start point commits the course of action and creates schedule pressure.
The labeled summary frames the database choice as an already-settled organizational decision, though the split footing makes it reported.
The labeled quantified benefit foregrounds technical expertise and evidence-based persuasion; the split footing makes it reported.
The labeled schedule fixes a migration deadline-like commitment and therefore carries pressure; the split footing makes it reported.
